# From session history to provider requests {#sec:message-formats}

A single user prompt travels through four different message representations
before a model sees it, and the answer travels back through three more. Each
representation is owned by a different layer, and each boundary is a place
where information is deliberately dropped or reshaped. This chapter names each
representation, shows the exact function that performs each conversion, and
explains which boundary an extension author should use for a given job.

## Prerequisites

Read [Sessions, trees, and
compaction](03-sessions-trees-compaction.qmd#sec:sessions) and
[Architecture](05-architecture-for-extensions.qmd#sec:architecture) first: you
should know what a session entry is, what the leaf pointer does, and which
package owns which layer. Terminology is in the
[glossary](20-glossary.qmd#sec:glossary).

Every path below is relative to the Pi monorepo root.

## Six representations, one conversation

The same conversation exists in these shapes at different moments:

| Representation | Defined in | Kind | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SessionEntry` | `packages/coding-agent/src/core/session-manager.ts` | TypeScript interface union, serialized as one JSONL line | Durable record: one node of the session tree on disk |
| `AgentMessage` | `packages/agent/src/types.ts` | Type union | Runtime transcript inside the agent loop; `Message` plus app-specific roles |
| `Message` | `packages/ai/src/types.ts` | Type union (`UserMessage \| AssistantMessage \| ToolResultMessage`) | Pi's provider-neutral canonical format |
| `Context` | `packages/ai/src/types.ts` | Interface (`systemPrompt`, `messages`, `tools`) | One complete provider request, before serialization |
| Wire payload | `packages/ai/src/api/*.ts` (e.g. `ChatCompletionMessageParam`, `MessageParam`) | Provider SDK types, serialized as the HTTP JSON body | What a specific provider API actually receives |
| `AssistantMessageEvent` | `packages/ai/src/types.ts` | Type union, streamed by `AssistantMessageEventStream` | Inbound protocol: one streamed provider response, normalized |

Two properties of this table matter more than any row:

1. **Every conversion is one-directional and lossy on purpose.** Durable-only
   fields (extension state, labels, thinking-level changes) never reach the
   provider; provider quirks (ID formats, role constraints) never leak back
   into the session file.
2. **None of the message formats are classes.** `SessionEntry`, `AgentMessage`,
   `Message`, `Context`, and `AssistantMessageEvent` are plain-object
   interfaces and type unions — data with no methods. You construct them as
   object literals (or with small factories such as
   `createCompactionSummaryMessage()`). The runtime classes in this story are
   only three: `SessionManager` owns the file, `Agent` owns the running loop,
   and `AssistantMessageEventStream` carries the response. There is no
   `Message` class to instantiate or subclass.

## From the session file to runtime messages {#sec:session-to-runtime}

### Parsing: tolerant by design

`parseSessionEntries()` in `session-manager.ts` splits the file on newlines
and `JSON.parse`s each line; **malformed lines are skipped, not fatal**
(`loadEntriesFromFile()` does the same while streaming the file in chunks).
The first line must be the `type: "session"` header; older files are migrated
in place to the current version (`CURRENT_SESSION_VERSION = 3`), which adds
the `id`/`parentId` tree structure and renames the old `hookMessage` role to
`custom`. The practical rule: read sessions through `SessionManager`, never
by assuming every line parses or matches the newest version.

### Selecting a branch: id/parentId, not line order

Every entry after the header shares the same base shape:

```ts
export interface SessionEntryBase {
  type: string;
  id: string;
  parentId: string | null;
  timestamp: string;
}
```

The file is append-only, but the *active conversation* is not "all lines in
order". `SessionManager` keeps a **leaf pointer**; context construction walks
`parentId` links from the leaf to the root and reverses the result
(`buildSessionPath()`). Entries on abandoned branches stay in the file but
are not on the path, so they never reach the model. The full tree mechanics
are in [Sessions, trees, and
compaction](03-sessions-trees-compaction.qmd#sec:sessions).

### Compaction: substituting a summary

`buildContextEntries()` applies the compaction boundary on top of that path.
When the path contains `compaction` entries, the latest one is kept as an
entry of its own, the summarized span before it is dropped, and entries from
`firstKeptEntryId` onward (plus everything after the compaction entry) are
retained. Nothing is deleted from the file — this is a projection, not an
edit.

### Projecting entries to messages

`sessionEntryToContextMessages()` converts one selected entry into zero or
more `AgentMessage`s. This is the first place the "not everything becomes
context" rule is enforced:

| Entry `type` | Becomes model context? | Projection |
|---|---|---|
| `message` | Yes | The stored `AgentMessage` passes through (null content repaired to `[]`) |
| `custom_message` | Yes | Converted to a `CustomMessage` via `createCustomMessage()` |
| `compaction` | Yes | Converted to a `CompactionSummaryMessage` |
| `branch_summary` | Yes | Converted to a `BranchSummaryMessage` |
| `thinking_level_change` | No | Restores loop state (thinking level), not a message |
| `model_change` | No | Restores loop state (model selection), not a message |
| `custom` | No | Durable extension state only (`pi.appendEntry()`); ignored here |
| `label` | No | Bookmark metadata for `/tree` |
| `session_info` | No | Display-name metadata |

`buildSessionContext()` ties it together: it walks the path once to recover
the current thinking level and model, then flat-maps the compaction-aware
entry list through `sessionEntryToContextMessages()`. The result is:

```ts
export interface SessionContext {
  messages: AgentMessage[];   // runtime transcript for the agent loop
  thinkingLevel: string;
  model: { provider: string; modelId: string } | null;
}
```

Note what just happened: nine entry kinds collapsed into messages plus two
settings. An extension's private `custom` entries survive resume and `/tree`
without ever consuming a token of model context.

## Pi's canonical message format {#sec:canonical-messages}

The `AgentMessage[]` list is still coding-agent-shaped — it can contain
`bashExecution`, `custom`, `branchSummary`, and `compactionSummary` roles,
added to the `agent` package's `CustomAgentMessages` interface by declaration
merging in `packages/coding-agent/src/core/messages.ts`. The provider layer
must not know about those. Pi's exchange format is the smaller `Message`
union in `packages/ai/src/types.ts`:

```ts
export type Message = UserMessage | AssistantMessage | ToolResultMessage;
```

Three roles, each a plain interface:

- **`UserMessage`** (`role: "user"`): `content` is a string or an array of
  `TextContent`/`ImageContent` blocks, plus a `timestamp`.
- **`AssistantMessage`** (`role: "assistant"`): `content` is an array of
  typed blocks — `TextContent`, `ThinkingContent` (with an optional
  `thinkingSignature` for replay), or `ToolCall`. It also carries `api`,
  `provider`, and `model` (which produced it), `usage` (token counts and
  cost), a `stopReason`, an optional `errorMessage`, and a `timestamp`.
  `stopReason` is one of `"stop"`, `"length"`, `"toolUse"`, `"error"`,
  `"aborted"`.
- **`ToolResultMessage`** (`role: "toolResult"`): `toolCallId`, `toolName`,
  `content` (text/image blocks), an `isError` flag, optional structured
  `details` for UI rendering, and a `timestamp`.

All timestamps are Unix milliseconds. Content blocks are discriminated unions
— every block has a `type` field (`"text"`, `"thinking"`, `"image"`,
`"toolCall"`), so a `switch` on `block.type` is exhaustive. This is why the
format can stay provider-neutral: reasoning, images, and tool calls are
first-class blocks, not provider-specific JSON fragments.

One invariant holds the format together: **every `ToolCall` block's `id`
must be answered by a `ToolResultMessage` whose `toolCallId` equals it.**
Providers enforce this pairing with hard errors, and Pi enforces it itself in
`transformMessages()` (below), which inserts synthetic `"No result provided"`
error results for orphaned calls rather than send an invalid transcript.

A `Context` is then exactly one request's worth of canonical state:

```ts
export interface Context {
  systemPrompt?: string;
  messages: Message[];   // the canonical union above
  tools?: Tool[];        // name, description, TypeBox parameter schema
}
```

## From canonical messages to provider JSON {#sec:canonical-to-wire}

The outbound chain has three stages, each in a different package.

**Stage 1: `convertToLlm` (coding-agent).** The agent loop never converts
messages itself; `AgentLoopConfig.convertToLlm`
(`packages/agent/src/types.ts`) is a required callback. Coding-agent wires it
to `convertToLlm()` in `core/messages.ts` (wrapped in `core/sdk.ts` to strip
images when configured). It is a pure projection:

- `user`, `assistant`, `toolResult` — pass through unchanged.
- `bashExecution` — becomes a user message whose text is
  `bashExecutionToText()`; skipped entirely when `excludeFromContext` is set
  (the `!!` prefix).
- `custom` — becomes a user message from its string or text/image content.
- `branchSummary` / `compactionSummary` — become user messages with the
  summary wrapped in an explanatory prefix/suffix.

Anything else is filtered out. The result is the canonical `Message[]`.

**Stage 2: shared normalization (`transformMessages`).** Every adapter under
`packages/ai/src/api/` first calls `transformMessages(context.messages,
model, normalizeToolCallId)` from `transform-messages.ts`. It is the last
provider-neutral pass and fixes up the transcript for the *target* model:

- Normalizes tool-call IDs when history crosses models (e.g. 400-character
  OpenAI Responses IDs into Anthropic's `^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,64}$` shape),
  remapping matching `toolCallId`s on results.
- Replaces images with a text placeholder when the target model has no
  vision input.
- Replays thinking blocks only for the same model that produced them;
  cross-model, they degrade to plain text or are dropped.
- Skips assistant messages whose `stopReason` is `"error"` or `"aborted"`,
  and inserts synthetic tool results for orphaned tool calls.

**Stage 3: adapter serialization.** The adapter's own `convertMessages()`
turns the normalized `Message[]` into provider SDK types. This is where the
canonical format's neutrality pays off: one tool-call exchange, two very
different wire shapes.

The canonical exchange — an assistant `ToolCall` block and its result:

```json
{"role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"toolCall","id":"call_1","name":"read","arguments":{"path":"README.md"}}], "...": "usage, stopReason, api/provider/model omitted"}
{"role":"toolResult","toolCallId":"call_1","toolName":"read","content":[{"type":"text","text":"# Pi\n..."}],"isError":false}
```

`openai-completions.ts` serializes it as an assistant message with a
`tool_calls` array (arguments **stringified**) followed by a dedicated
`role: "tool"` message keyed by `tool_call_id`:

```json
{"role":"assistant","content":null,"tool_calls":[{"id":"call_1","type":"function","function":{"name":"read","arguments":"{\"path\":\"README.md\"}"}}]}
{"role":"tool","tool_call_id":"call_1","content":"# Pi\n..."}
```

`anthropic-messages.ts` serializes the same exchange as a `tool_use` content
block (arguments as a structured `input` object), with the result moved into
a **`tool_result` block inside a user-role message**:

```json
{"role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"call_1","name":"read","input":{"path":"README.md"}}]}
{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"tool_result","tool_use_id":"call_1","content":[{"type":"text","text":"# Pi\n..."}],"is_error":false}]}
```

Three structural differences — arguments as string vs. object, a `tool` role
vs. a `user`-wrapped block, `tool_call_id` vs. `tool_use_id` — are absorbed
entirely by the adapter. Nothing above `Context` changes, and the session
file keeps the single canonical form regardless of which model is active;
[Models, providers, and
authentication](12-models-providers-and-auth.qmd#sec:models) covers how the
adapter itself is selected.

## From provider response to session entry {#sec:wire-to-session}

The inbound direction mirrors the outbound one:

1. **Adapter translation.** The adapter consumes the provider's stream (SSE
   chunks or WebSocket frames) and pushes normalized `AssistantMessageEvent`s
   — `start`, then `text_delta`/`thinking_delta`/`toolcall_delta` chunks,
   `toolcall_end`, and finally `done` or `error`. Each event carries the
   growing `partial` assistant message, so consumers never parse provider
   JSON.
2. **The event stream.** `AssistantMessageEventStream`
   (`packages/ai/src/utils/event-stream.ts`) is the one runtime class on this
   path: an async-iterable queue of `AssistantMessageEvent`s whose `result()`
   promise resolves to the final `AssistantMessage` — the `message` of a
   `done` event or the `error` of an `error` event. The stream contract
   forbids throwing: failures arrive as an `error` event carrying an
   assistant message with `stopReason: "error"` (or `"aborted"`) and
   `errorMessage` set.
3. **Agent events.** The loop in `packages/agent` iterates the stream with
   `for await` and re-emits `message_start`, `message_update` (carrying the
   `assistantMessageEvent`), and `message_end`, then appends the finished
   `AssistantMessage` to its state. See [Prompt
   lifecycle](07-lifecycle-and-hooks.qmd#sec:prompt-lifecycle) and [Agent
   core](13-agent-core.qmd#sec:agent-core) for the full event ordering.
4. **Persistence.** `AgentSession` handles `message_end`
   (`packages/coding-agent/src/core/agent-session.ts`): ordinary messages go
   to `SessionManager.appendMessage()`, extension-injected custom messages to
   `appendCustomMessageEntry()`. Either way a new JSONL line is appended as a
   child of the current leaf — closing the loop back to the representation
   this chapter started with. Note that even a failed turn's assistant
   message is persisted (its `errorMessage` is part of the record);
   `transformMessages()` skips it when building the *next* request, so the
   model retries from the last valid state.

## Choosing the right boundary {#sec:choose-boundary}

Each representation answers different questions. Work at the highest layer
that truthfully has the data you need:

| You want to... | Work with | At | See |
|---|---|---|---|
| Inspect or repair history, branches, or durable extension state | `SessionEntry` / `SessionManager` | The JSONL file and `core/session-manager.ts` | [Sessions, trees, and compaction](03-sessions-trees-compaction.qmd#sec:sessions) |
| Add a message kind the UI renders but the model may or may not see | `AgentMessage` via declaration merging, plus `convertToLlm` | `core/messages.ts` | [Architecture](05-architecture-for-extensions.qmd#sec:architecture) |
| Change what the model sees per request (prune, inject) | `AgentMessage[]` in a `context` handler / `transformContext` | Extension hooks | [Prompt lifecycle](07-lifecycle-and-hooks.qmd#sec:prompt-lifecycle), [Extension event reference](18-extension-event-reference.qmd#sec:events) |
| Change canonical message semantics for every consumer | `Message`, `Context` | `packages/ai/src/types.ts` | [Agent core](13-agent-core.qmd#sec:agent-core) |
| Inspect or replace the exact bytes sent to a provider | The wire payload via `before_provider_request` | Extension provider hooks | [Models, providers, and authentication](12-models-providers-and-auth.qmd#sec:models) |
| Support a genuinely new wire protocol | A new adapter next to `openai-completions.ts` / `anthropic-messages.ts` | `packages/ai/src/api/` | [Guided source tours](17-guided-source-tours.qmd#sec:tours) |
| Render streaming output | `AssistantMessageEvent` via `message_update` | Extension/TUI layer | [Extension event reference](18-extension-event-reference.qmd#sec:events) |

Two rules of thumb cover most mistakes:

- **Durable state never crosses the provider boundary by accident.** If
  extension data must influence the model, inject it as a `custom_message`
  entry or a `context` handler; `pi.appendEntry()` alone keeps it private.
- **Provider JSON never leaks upward.** If you find yourself switching on
  `tool_calls` vs. `tool_use` outside `packages/ai/src/api/`, the logic
  belongs in an adapter.

## Beginner checkpoint

Name the representation and the converting function for each step:

1. A resumed session's file becomes the runtime transcript.
2. The transcript becomes the provider-neutral request messages.
3. Canonical messages become Anthropic's `tool_use`/`tool_result` JSON.
4. A streamed provider response becomes a persisted assistant message.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Solution

1. `SessionEntry` lines to `AgentMessage[]`, via `buildSessionContext()`
   (parsing, branch walk, compaction, `sessionEntryToContextMessages()`).
2. `AgentMessage[]` to `Message[]` inside a `Context`, via the coding-agent
   `convertToLlm()` in `core/messages.ts`.
3. `Message[]` to wire JSON, via `transformMessages()` then the adapter's
   `convertMessages()` in `packages/ai/src/api/anthropic-messages.ts`.
4. Provider chunks to `AssistantMessageEvent`s on an
   `AssistantMessageEventStream`, then `message_end` triggers
   `SessionManager.appendMessage()` — a new JSONL `message` entry.

If you can place each conversion in its owning package, the pipeline is
working.
:::
